title: overlay graph
description: Shape of components/kg-content/entities/graphs/<slug>.json -- a named set of typed, directed relationships over entities that already exist elsewhere in kg-content. See SCHEMA.md's 'Overlay graphs' section for the governing rule (reference, never restate) and decision 35 for why this type exists. No automated validator wired up yet (stdlib-only convention; skipping a jsonschema dependency rather than breaking it -- see kg-core/README.md).

schema_version.description: Marked -experimental while the overlay-graph shape is still provisional. Only one overlay exists, so nothing has yet tested whether a second would fit.

description.description: A short, plain-language overview of what the graph shows and what question it answers -- what a viewer displays under its title (decision 67). Curated like the rest of the file; not derived from `stages` or `nodes`.

owner.description: Role, never a personal name -- see CLAUDE.md's no-personal-names rule.

source.description: Where this graph originated. Authoritative only while `provenance` is `derived`; once it is `curated-here`, this is historical origin and the file itself is the source of truth.

provenance.description: Which copy governs (decision 61). `derived`: the graph mirrors `source`, and differences are extraction errors to fix here. `curated-here`: this file is the source of truth and is iterated on directly in git; `source` is not re-synced, and differences from it are expected. Absent means `derived`, the original assumption.

source_notes.description: Required in practice whenever `source` is not directly machine-readable, so a reader can tell what was transcribed from where. The first overlay's source is a Confluence whiteboard whose body the Atlassian connector cannot fetch at all.

stages.description: Ordered phases of the modelled flow. Consumers may use `ordinal` for layout and for deciding which arcs are feedback.

items.description: Either `domain_ref` (and then NO restated domain facts) or `kind` + `title` for something the domain model does not cover. Enforcing that either/or is a validation rule, not expressible cleanly here -- see SCHEMA.md.

domain_ref.description: An id in domains.json. Title, category, purpose and scope are resolved from there at read time and must NOT be duplicated here.

title.description: Only for nodes without a `domain_ref`. A title alongside a `domain_ref` is a restated domain fact and a bug.

responsibility.description: What this node does *in this flow specifically* -- distinct from the domain's own `purpose`, which stays in domains.json.

touchpoints.description: Concrete endpoints collapsed into this node rather than modelled as separate nodes, because no edge addresses them individually. Kept lean on purpose.

predicate.description: SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE. Deliberately NOT a controlled vocabulary yet -- the first overlay uses 36 distinct predicates and there is no second overlay to show which recur. A controlled vocabulary is what cross-overlay contradiction detection would need; see SCHEMA.md's open item.

payload.description: What actually crosses the edge. Required, because an untyped arrow is the thing this schema exists to prevent.

stage.description: Must match a `stages[].id`. May differ from either endpoint's stage; a cross-stage edge is the interesting case.
